why_lead: XRP closed at 2.94 after rising 34.07% in the prior completed daily close and 21.23% over 20 sessions, with Solana up 24.23% in the same session, so the price move and the headlines coincide on the same naming event. The retail attention is explicit (Stocktwits flagged Solana retail sentiment at a year low on February 25, Axios tied the rally to Truth Social posts, and meme-coin coverage ran both ways), and the story is simple enough for the crowd to repeat.
why_smaller: Tesla is down 26.81% over 20 sessions while protests against Musk and Barron’s $700 bull case keep the stock in the retail conversation.
IonQ is down 36.69% over 20 sessions while a 24/7 Wall St. million-dollar headline and quantum-theme coverage keep the story in the retail conversation.
SOXL is down 16.28% over 20 sessions while CNBC’s leveraged-ETF appetite headlines and the Korean leveraged-ETF losses give an instrument-level narrative that differs from the single-name trades.
considered_not_chosen: Palantir / PLTR: the five-session drop of 16.21% comes with headlines that its biggest fans are leaving (Yahoo, Feb 28) rather than buying, and the 20-session change is still +4.56%, so the crowd is exiting rather than buying a drawdown.

Rocket Lab / RKLB: a short-report drawdown of 28.18% over 20 sessions with a real retail story, but the attention is a governance fight with a launch date rather than a crowd trade, so it went to the catalysts section.
Super Micro / SMCI: a filing-relief surge that fell 26.06% over five sessions (market card); a single-company event used in the earnings pattern instead of the retail section.

Gold and silver: Americans-buying-gold and Costco-gold headlines exist, but the card shows gold down 3.55% and silver down 5.33% over five sessions, so there is no surge or dip-buying price evidence to lead with.
Hims & Hers: a 22% plunge on margin and compounding concerns, which is a sell-off rather than a crowd buying the drawdown; used in the Lilly and healthcare notes.

Nuclear and AI-power names (Oklo, NuScale, Nano Nuclear, Vistra): strong headline flow, but the price evidence shows a rotation toward natural gas (WSJ, Mar 1), which weakens the crowd narrative; used in the utilities block.
